# Original camera lifecycle and cleanup oracle

Expected values are captured by executing unchanged original camera lifecycle
and cleanup helpers, with checker/helper SHA256 and CPython provenance. The
process fixture contains all 32 ordinary cases, two smoke selections, eight
cleanup cases, repeated case filtering, and 43 original-main process/failure
boundaries. Its subprocess peer controls only observations, preserving actual
original resource audit, ownership, image, result, report and exception code.
Temporary namespace suffixes alone are projected to `$NAMESPACE`; root paths
are projected to `$ROOT`. Each namespace is checked alive during the child and
absent after completion/error. Disk free is controlled independently; exact
26 GiB boundary and one-byte failure remain captured.

104 generic helper captures cover image identity/payload rewriting, f32 event
conversion, missing/type/value errors, all resource ledger categories, disabled
cleanup envelopes and error controls. Eight real CLI captures preserve output
creation phases. Existing current-source C++ versus Rust reports pass 32 regular
and eight cleanup cases; each receipt's three current binary hashes were
independently checked before reuse. This is historical evidence reuse, not a
new native comparator run.

The native comparator uses native ISP normalization; the runtime checker still
imports Python cleanup audit, so that helper remains pending. The lifecycle CLI,
kernel digest/core helper, ISP helper and three-case artifact-path Python test
are retired after migrating their callers and assertions. Child environment
removal uses the shared authoritative env_remove API.
Capture scripts are ignored under
`.analysis/scratch/2026-10-18-camera-lifecycle-check/`. Seven native tests and scoped strict Clippy pass, including three exact original
portable-path receipts and a real raw-path/inherited-stdin/environment-removal
child. The current native comparator passes all 32 regular and eight cleanup
cases with PATH disabled. Full reports equal independent originals except for
the separately measured free_bytes value, which retains its 26 GiB guard.
These are host fixture checks, not device acceptance.
